source_observations.observation: The neighbouring verse contains a prohibition. The clause containing raghūttamam in 7.101 instead has modayadhvam. At 7.102 the monkeys depart.
Addressed plural group, beneficiary of the undertaking, fear and the Sītā clause have distinct roles.
Expressly takes the first predicate under 3.3.132 and explains the second by harṣayata. Gives an indication-of-fear reading, then acquisition in a marital sense.

source_observations.locator: Jayamaṅgalā, Bāpata edition, Bombay 1887, manuscript scan b3009303x, printed pp. 184–185
source_observations.observation: Same four explanatory clauses. The web OCR misreads several verb clusters. The separate verse transcript and second commentary edition supply the positive readings.
Root-final m participates in the optional kit history for the aorist.
Objectless sam plus gam takes the middle. The adjacent phrase locating the meeting does not supply a transitive object.
A prospective wish permits forms otherwise used of the past. The commentary applies this to the meeting before the enemy.
The entry gives causal modayati. It separately lists the curādi contact verb with matching stem letters.

source_observations.locator: Pāṇini 3.1.26, hetumati ca, with causal middle 1.3.74
source_observations.observation: The causal adds a causer. The verse itself warrants the middle ending. A unique actor-benefit inference is left open.
Signalling and taking in marriage differ in sic-kit status. PG86 records the optional marriage forms.

source_observations.locator: Nyāsānusandhāna on Haima 3.3.86 pp. 244–245, digital pages 234–235
source_observations.observation: Inherited PG361. The quoted han has a first-person participant in both supplied ellipses. These are distinct from the mud object of 7.101.
In this particular episode the returned charioteer, king’s grief and death, mourners and envoys are narrated. This episode supplies no quoted plural address matching S1.
